result.title: Auditing Tool Traces in Agentic LLMs: Source Localization and Counterfactual Dependence Testing
result.comment: 12 pages. Accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Agentic AI for Biological Discovery (AgenticLS)
result.summary: Agentic LLMs increasingly support scientific prediction by grounding decisions in external evidence. In biology, they promise accurate, interpretable predictions for important problems by integrating complex experimental and computational evidence. However, serialized tool results can contain hidden label shortcuts, such as dataset identifiers or template artifacts, that create apparent success without biological reasoning. To address this risk, we introduce a two-stage audit. Stage 1, Per-Tool TF-IDF Decomposition (PT2D), localizes label-predictive patterns to individual tool results while avoiding signal dilution in the concatenated tool trace. Stage 2, Token-Class Redaction, counterfactually tests whether the frozen LLM depends on the localized shortcut. We apply this audit to TCR-pMHC binding, where tool augmentation substantially outperforms a no-evidence baseline. At face value, this suggests that the LLM has learned to use scientific evidence. The audit overturns this interpretation: PT2D localizes the strongest signal to identifiers in one tool result, and redacting them reduces performance to chance. These findings show how hidden label shortcuts can masquerade as scientific reasoning or discovery, motivating source-level audits before benchmark gains are trusted.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出两阶段审计流程：先用 Per-Tool TF-IDF Decomposition 把串联工具输出中具有标签预测性的片段定位到单个工具结果，再用 Token-Class Redaction 做反事实测试；在 TCR-pMHC 结合预测上发现模型实际依赖数据集标识符等隐藏捷径，遮蔽后性能跌回随机水平。
AI.relevance_reason: 该文把「答案是否真正使用外部证据、还是被捷径旁路」做成可定位加反事实遮蔽的检验流程，可能为核查 VLM 推理是否真的使用视觉证据、以及证据贡献分配提供方法线索，可供人工复核其可迁移性。
